abstract: The paper deals with an investigation on the capacitive and inductive switching capability of grounding switches, as required for parallel HVAC transmission lines with one circuit carrying the current while the other is grounded at both ends. When the grounding switches are opened, they have to interrupt both the induced inductive current, and the current coupled capacitively. In addition, they have to withstand the transient recovery voltage (TRV).

articleTitle: Blackstart Utilization of Remote Combustion Turbines, Analytical Analysis and Field Test
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper illustrates that some special operating procedures may be needed to blackstart a generating station from a remote combustion turbine generator. A method is presented to determine what, if any, special procedures are needed for a specific case. The results of a blackstart field test on an actual system are then compared to the analytical analysis.

articleTitle: The Application of N-Phase Generalized Rotating Field Theory to Induction Machines with Arbitrary Stator Winding Connection
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: N-phase theory applicable to the calculation of the steady state performance of squirrel cage induction motors with arbitrary staor winding connection is presented. The internal voltage equations of the machine incorporate the effects of space harmonics, different turns ratios and angular asymmetry, while the external voltage and current equations incorporate a connection matrix which defines the specific winding arrangement.

articleTitle: On-Line Real Power Scheduling in Marginally Secure Power Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: In this paper an efficient algorithm is derived for scheduling real power in systems where the phase angles across lines are not small and, hence, have to be taken into consideration. The approach is based on assigning a cost to the loading on the transmission system. The cost lunction chosen in this paper simplifies the problem of scheduling to a load-flow type problem so that when the solution to the load- flow problem is obtained, the optimal dispatch solution is also automatically obtained. Thus there is no need to alternate between a load-flow step and an optimization step and this results in considerable computational savings.

articleTitle: Three Dimensional Modelling Of HV Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The Numerical Electromagnetics Code (NEC) is applied to frequency-domain modelling of HV systems. This application results in an improved model in comparison with the lumped-distributed approach. The new model not only takes into account the geometry of each individual piece of apparatus but also includes the effect of coupling between different components of the HV system. The model additionally incorporates the effects of parasitic elements such as the inductance of a resistive divider or ground plane losses. The limitations and capabilities of the user-oriented implementation of the NEC in the analysis of HV systems are presented by modelling a few of the following problems: the electromagnetic interference (EMI) generated by discharging an RV impulse generator, the transfer function of a resistive divider, and the electromagnetic (EM) field distribution of a resistive divider.

articleTitle: Switching of Capacitive Currents by Disconnectors in Gas Insulated Substations
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Tests on the subject of switching capacitive currents by disconnectors in Gas Insulated Substations have been carried out with various test objects and arrangements. This paper deals with the phenomena which occur during the switching operation. The causes of the transients and the increase in field strength are described by reference to the tests performed. The influence of various test parameters such as: voltage, gas pressure concentrated or distributed capacitances is shown.

articleTitle: Effect of Surge Capacitor Lead Length on Protection of Motors from Steep Switching Surges
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The results reported in this paper suggest that capacitor protection of large AC motors may not be adequate to protect against motor starting switching surges when the length of the leads connecting the capacitor to the machine terminals and to ground are substantial. Accordingly, it is shown that the magnitude and shape of the switching surges appearing in the machine windings depend upon the length of the capacitor connecting leads. It is shown that steep switching surges with high rates of rise can be impressed on motor winding insulation when the surge capacitor leads to machine terminals and to ground are long.

articleTitle: Prediction Of The Optimum coupling For PLC Propagation On Double Circuit And High Phase Order Transmission Lines
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The characteristics and performance of the 'Power Line Carrier' digital program are described. Accurate simulation models and efficient propagation algorithms permit fast computation of the voltage attenuation of coupling connections on single-circuit, double-circuit or high-phase order lines. The lossy transmission systems may have discontinuity points due to phase-transpositions, series or shunt circuits with lumped parameters, terminal impedances or shunt-faults. Voltage attenuation of line-to-line and line-to-ground coupling connections is computed as a function of frequency for horizontal and vertical double-circuit lines and for a six-phase line. A sensitivity analysis of the carrier channel attenuation is performed with respect to variations of the average height of the conductors above the ground plane, of the conductor stranding factor, the earth resistivity and the terminal impedances in the case of the double-circuit vertical line. The comparative analysis of the results obtained proposes the best couplings for each line considered.

articleTitle: Performance Parameters of Power Transformers Using 3D Magnetic Field Calculations
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Today's challenges in the design of power transformers necessitate, among other things, very accurate calculation of the performance parameters of the transformer (such as losses, impedance, shielding, s.c. forces, etc.), reduction of load losses, and preventing overheating and local hot spots. Presented in this paper are theoretical and experimental studies conducted to precisely assess the need and projected benefits of these calculations based on the 3D determination of the leakage field of the transformer. Also presented are results of the already achieved objectives in winding loss calculation and magnetic shielding design.

articleTitle: Development of a Prototype UHV Transformer and its Application to 500 kV Transformers
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Development principles of an insulation structure for a prototype UHV transformer are presented. New interleaved windings having gradual apportionment of series capacitances were developed, and shown to have approximately uniform voltage distribution for lightning impulse and high reliabaility in their dielectric characteristics. The insulation structure developed for the UHV transformer was applied to a 500 kV transforrner, which allowed its floor space, weight and loss to be reduced about 20 % compared to a conventional 500 kV transformer.

articleTitle: Investigation Of Soil Resistivity Measuring Techniques Using An Electrolytic Tank
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper presents the results of an experimental investigation of the interpretive techniques of soil resistivity measurements. An electrolytic tank with various two-layer soil structures was used. The soil structure can be determined if the proper measurement parameters are met; however, a subjective evaluation may be necessary in some cases.

articleTitle: Cold Start Performance of Transformers Filled With High Molecular Weight Hydrocarbon Liquid
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Two high loss 167 kVA pole type transformers were filled with conventional mineral oil and cold start tested at -30°C under full load. The two units were subsequently drained, retrofilled with a high molecular weight hydrocarbon (HMWH) fluid, and then retested at -30°C. The units were identical, except one used corrugated fins for cooling and the other used radiator panels. Thermocouple temperature readings indicated that the units were successfully cold started with both types of fluid. When filled with MWH fluid, maximum winding temperatures of 58°C and 52°C were recorded for the finned and radiator transformers, respectively. These winding temperatures are well below the 105°C maximum continuous rating of the insulation (65°C rise over a 40 ° C ambient). No thermal runaway occurred. Ideed,den- the results indicate that HMWH filled transformers can tolerate substantial overloads during both startup and continuous operation at low ambient temperatures.

articleTitle: Electric Stresses in an HVDC Cable Through Joint
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Longitudinal and radial stresses in a hvdc cable through joint are computed using a finite difference method. The joint and associated cable are rated at 266 kV d. c., 1200A and assumed buried to a depth of l.lm in homogeneous soil of thermal resistivity 1.2 deg C-m W-1. Initially the temperature distribution is determined and the node to node finite difference resistances in the electrical representation calculated using the relationship, σ= σexp(αθ+ ßE) with an assumed voltage and stress distribution. A revised stress distribution is then computed, the nodal resistances adjusted to the new stresses and the iterative process repeated until the nodal voltage changes are below a prescribed limit.

articleTitle: Pyrotechnique Circuit Interrupter for the Protection of Electrical Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The theory of operation and performance of the Ferraz current limiting pyrotechnique circuit interrupter for the protection of low and medium voltage electrical systems is described. This protective system consists of three major parts, a sensor, a control circuit and a pyrobreaker. The desired quantity, current, dl/dt, temperature, light etc., is monitored using the sensing circuit. The signal generated by the sensor is compared against a preset reference in the control circuit. When a fault occurs in the protected electrical system, an error signal is produced in the control circuit which results in the triggering of the pyrobreaker that finally interrupts the circuit. The pyrobreaker consists of two main components, a specially designed copper conductor that can carry large continuous currents and that can be sheared at high speed by pyro- breaking technique, and a current limiting fuse mounted in parallel with this conductor. When a fault is detected, the conductor is opened at high speed (the shearing of the conductor occurs in 100 Ls to 150 μs;, and the current is commutated to the parallel fuse which then interrupts the circuit providing current limiting protection. This system offers the advantage of carrying high continuous currents up to 10 KA at low and medium voltages, while providing current limiting protection in electrical systems where short circuit currents can be in excess of 50 KA to 75 KA.

articleTitle: Television Interference due to Electromagnetic Scattering by the MOD-2 Wind Turbine Generators
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The characterization and identification of electromagnetic interference created by the slowly rotating blade of a MOD-2 wind turbine generator (WTG) is investigated. Field measurement data supports the thesis that at ground level the near field scattered component is an amplitude modulated secondary signal. A prediction methodology to define zones of interference to television broadcast reception is presented.

articleTitle: Distributed Intelligence Load Control: Yes or No?
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper summarizes the key points of discussion raised during a panel session sponsored by the Power Systems Engineering Committee at the Summer Power Meeting in Los Angeles, July 17-22, 1983. The panel examined the trend in information processing toward distributed intelligence for decision making and the impact of this trend on load control programs. The question was raised, "Should this trend toward distributed intelligence in information processing be extended to load control?" A regulator noted that distributed intelligence could help provide rate options for controlling customer's costs. A utility system operator said that some type of telecommunications link to any load controller was essential. A utility consultant said that distributed intelligence could improve the operating characteristics of existing centrally controlled systems. A utility researcher said that distributed intelligence load control programs would be more successful by being more sensitive to the variations in customers' appliance use--at negligible incremental cost.

articleTitle: A Review of 1983 Dispatchable Load Management Operations at Pacific Gas and Electric Co.
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Results of operations of a large, diversified dispatchable load management program are reviewed. Preliminary results from Summer 1983 indicate consistent levels of aggregate load relief in the range 130-180 MW can be obtained from a dispatchable load management program of the size described. Issues for further study and refinement of dispatchable load management are briefly outlined.

articleTitle: Computation of Frequency of Severe Power System Faults
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: An analytical procedure is introduced to compute the frequency of single and multi-phase faults normally cleared or with delayed clearing at or near a major switching station. Data requirements are discussed and numerical examples are presented illustrating the method.

articleTitle: Influence of Earthquakes and Other Loads on the Layout of Gas-Insulated Substations
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The mechanics of a Gas-Insulated Substation are a complicated problem, which can have a considerable influence on the layout of the equipment as well as on the supporting structure and foundation. Rather few papers dealing with this problem have been published. It is our experience that those concerned with selecting GIS-layouts not always are aware of all the precautions and considerations that have to be taken for mechanical reasons. Of the various forces that have to be taken into account the thermal and seismic loads usually have the greatest influence on the layout. Most of the loads that affect the substation will also have influence on the building and foundation. In this paper thermal loads, seismic loads and reaction forces from circuit-breakers are described in more detail, as well as methods to design with respect to these loads.

articleTitle: Surge Protection of Motors - Is it Sufficient?
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper presents a guideline for motor surge protection policy as a result of failure investigation of a 9000 HP induction motor, which was adequately protected by surge arresters and capacitors.

articleTitle: Calculation of Loss in Solid-Salient-Pole Machine
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: For the critical design of a solid-salient-pole machine, it is necessary to calculate the losses accurately. In this paper, the losses in a solid-salient-pole machine under asynchronous operation are calculated using the finite element method (FEM). The results of calculation are generalized so that the designer can accurately estimate losses over the pole surfaces of a solid-salient-pole machine without using FEM every time.

articleTitle: Steady-State Stability Analysis with Frequency Methods: Optimization of Excitation System Parameters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: In this paper analysis of the steady-state stability of a large power network is conducted using frequency methods. The problem of selecting the appropriate values of excitation system parameters (e. g., regulator and power system stabilizer gains) for a multimachine power system is considered. A procedure for optimizing these adjustable parameters, to give the best degree of stability at the desired frequency range, is presented.

articleTitle: Harmonic Current Interruption Phenomena In ARC Furnace Filter Circuits
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The current interruption phenomenon in arc filter circuit containing harmonic current was experimented in the field and analyzed by TNA (Transient Network Analyzer) and numerical analysis to calculate the recovery voltage. The recovery voltage when the filter circuit contains harmonic current becomes greater than that obtained in the IEC-specified test using a small leading current.

articleTitle: Development of Digitalized Control Equipment for the HVDC Transmission System
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: As the necessity for long distance large power transmission increases, the need for higher reliability and higher performance HVDC control equipment increases.

articleTitle: A Model Advanced Electric Power Engineering Curriculum
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper constitutes the final report of the Task Force on Electric Power Engineering Curriculmn to the Power Engineering Education Committee of the IEEE Power Engineering Society. The report describes a Model Advanped Electric Power Engineering Curriculum. Details of the curriculum are provided.

articleTitle: Application Of A System To Monitor The Conductor Temperature Of Underground Cables
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A computer method to allow control and prediction of pipe type cable conductor temperatures by the system operator, has been developed and implemented in the Florida Power and Light Company system. The programs used are part of a real-time operating computer network. Through the use of a well established thermal modeling technique and transmitted cable insulation shield temperatures and recorded conductor currents, accurate conductor temperatures have been calculated.

articleTitle: Air-Cored Alternators: A Numerical-Analytical Transient Field Model
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The paper presents detailed analysis of the field patterns in superconducting alternators which, because of removal of the iron magnetic paths, are quite different from those of conventional machines. Special consideration has been given to the rotor screen and methods of measuring and predicting its parameters have been described. Attempt has been made to justify work done with experimental results.

articleTitle: Microprocessor-Based Controllers and an Intelligent Capacitor-Bank Controller
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The power industry is at a point in its evolution where sophisticated control decisions. will have to be executed to enable systems to run with the utmost of efficiency. In order to incorporate the equipment needed to effect these decision processes, engineers designing these systems need to know some specific details with regard to microprocessor-based controls, such as the intellegent capacitor-bank controller described in this article. They need to have an understanding of the abilities and limitations of such equipment in order that wise judgements may be made in achieving the goals of the industry.

articleTitle: Requirements for a Transformerless Power Conditioning Subsystem
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The interconnection of a photovoltaic generator to a utility can be made more cost effective by eliminating the need for an isolation or dedicated utility transformer.

articleTitle: Analysis of Re-Ignition of Multiple Break Switches Devices Application to Shunt Reactor Current Interruption
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The interruption of shunt reactor current has been studied on a Hydro-Quebec substation. The study describes the test results basedon particular characterlstics of the circuit breaker: the influence of the auxiliary chamber synchrcnism and the influence of the opening resistor values of the breaker arefirst recorded. Their theoretical models are then developed to appraise the trqrlsient voltage across the breaker terminals and the overvoltages phenomena experienced. The re-ignition, phenomena is then modeled according to the CIGRE Working Group 13-02 Recommendatatives and, a good correlation between the test results and the models output are confirmed.

articleTitle: Technical Overview Through Development of the Largest Scale Turbine-Generator Model with Full Water Cooling
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Although turbine-generators have recently achieved larger rated output, higher efficiency, and high reliability, it is necessary to continue research and development for further refinement. TOSHIBA has developed a multipurpose full scale generator model simulating a 2000 MVA generator which is predicted as the manufacturable maximum limit for a 3600 r/min machine. This model has the same dimensions as a 2000 MVA generator, but its core length is shortened to one third of the full-length generator. All tests scheduled have been completed successfully. This is a fully water-cooled generator with the maximum diameter rotor for a 3600 r/min machine and has ratings of 30 kV class terminal voltage and 40 kA class armature current. This paper describes the outline of the model and its test results and also shows trends of generator design including the manufacturable limit and its limiting factors.

articleTitle: Pre-Insullation Testing and Installation Experience with a Fiber-Optic Cored Shield Wire on a Rochester Gas and Electric Corporation 115 KV Transmission Line
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A 5,000 meter fiber optic channel integral to the ground wire of a 115 kV transmission line has been installed and is operational. Rochester Gas and Electric Corporation (RG&E) has installed a composite overhead conductor manuf'actured by Phillips Cables Limited between two major transmission stations to provide communications for protection, metering, and control. This paper discusses the economic justification, equipment, construction techniques, and testing associated with the installation and commissioning.

articleTitle: Late discussion and closure to "Load-Flow Solutions for Ill-Conditioned Power Systems by a Newton-Like Method"
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems

articleTitle: Bibliography on Distribution Automation 1969-1982
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A bibliography of 161 articles on distribution automation is presented. The articles referenced cover the period from 1969 through 1982 and represent publications originating in North America. The bibliography is presented in two parts. The first part gives a listing by year of the references. The second part gives a subject organization for the bibliography and a cross-index by subject.

articleTitle: Transmisson Line Route Selection: An Application Of K-Shortest Paths And Goal Programming
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A two-stage solution procedure is developed as a managerial decision making tool in the transmission line route selection process. In stage one, the K least costly alternatives are found, based strictly on monetary considerations. In stage two, the alternative which causes the least amount of social and environmental disruption is selected from the alternatives generated in stage one.

articleTitle: Some New Algorithms for Staff Estimation in Power Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper presents three improved methods to solve the static state estimation problem of power systems. Thp first method presents a modified fast decoupled state estimator which is faster than the fast decoupled state estimator available in the literature. The second method is based on a new constant matrix model which is more reliable than the fast decoupled state estimator. The third method is based on a second order load flow model. The proposed methods are tested on different IEEE test systems and relevant results are presented to illustrate the same.

articleTitle: Shield-Interrupt Overvoltages On 138-KV Extruded Dielectric Cables
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Special shield-bonding techniques have been used on underground transmission cables to minimize the circulating currents in the shields which, in turn, reduce the loss and heating effects. The techniques used on extruded dielectric cables can result in a very economical cable installation. However, the shield interrupts, where the special bonding takes place, have been a source of problems to the industry because these shields have been subjected to excessive overvoltages. This work defines the overvoltages that may be seen at shield interrupts on 138-kV extruded dielectric cable systems over a wide range of system conditions.

articleTitle: Breakdown of a Coaxial-Cylinder Gap in SF6 Under Switching Impulse Voltages
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The paper constitutes an experimental investigation into the impulse voltage strength of a coaxial-cylinder gap in SF6. Impulse voltage waves of both polarities and different fronts were applied at the gap at different pressures. In each case the fifty percent breakdown voltage was determined and plotted according to the pressure for a given wave front and according to the wave front at a given pressure. An approach of the breakdown mechanisms is then developped for explaining the trend of the obtained curves.

articleTitle: Measured Interconnected Behavior of Wind Turbine Inverters
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Distribution engineers are concerned about harmonic currents injected in the distribution network by switching inverters and load controls. When an inverter is driven by a random power source such as a windmill or photo voltaic array, the effects may be exacerbated due to second by second power output variations due to the source as well as the cycle by cycle distortion due to switching semi-conductors in the inverter. During a performance measurement program on nearly 20 consumer-owner wind turbines in Michigan, the authors' had the opportunity to record the harmonic, var, and voltage behavior of several single- phase line-commutated inverters supplied with variable- speed wind-turbine generators.

articleTitle: Measurements of Transmission Line Electric Fields in a Residential Environment
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Typical cbjects in the residential environrent are suspected to provide sufficient shielding to significantly reduce the strength of electric fields produced by nearby transmission lines below the levels calculated by mast analytical techniques. Yet, there is little support found in published materials to substantiate this point. This paper presents measurements of actual field strength in such areas and compares them to calculated values. Data such as those reported herein are necessary to accurately assess human exposure to electric fields.

articleTitle: Distributed Control Messages, Their Security and Efficiency
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Message integrity and efficiency are essential features of distributed control systems.

articleTitle: Surface Breakdown Characteristics of Rubber Insulating Gloves Exposed Outdoors
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Surface flashover and tracking breakdown tests were carried out on rubber insulating gloves under various relative humidities and fog and rain conditions, and on gloves which have been exposed outdoors for various periods of time. When gloves are exposed outdoors, cracks and recesses form on the glove surfaces. Direct exposure to rain and fog has a noticeable effect on the flashover voltage. With an increase in the period of exposure outdoors, the time to tracking breakdown decreases.

articleTitle: An Innovative Approach to High Voltage Engineering Education and Research
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Power engineering education is faced with the challenge of the environmental problems that the power industry has experienced in recent years. One of the most important environmental issues to the nation, the power industry and power engineering education is the question currently being raised regarding high voltage transmission lines. This paper describes an approach to deal with these environmental problems from both education and research points of view. This approach has been found to be highly successful in educating students, farmers, managers, engineers and the general public about high voltage transmission systems.

articleTitle: A Combustion Monitoring and Evaluation System for Large Utility Boilers
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A combustion monitoring and evaluation system, with a microcomputer, for large scale boilers in thermal power plants has been developed. This system can determine indices, such as impurity concentrations of NOx and CO, temperatures of heaters and burner impellers, thermal efficiency, etc. Standard values of these twelve indices necessary for proper operation, as well as the allowed upper and lower limit values, are shown in concentric circles on a color CRT. Measured index values are superimposed on the concentric circles in the form of a polygon. By comparison between measured and standard values, operators can determine the boiler combustion condition. When values of any index exeed the allowed limit values, an alarm signal is sent to the CRT with relevant messages indicating where to check. In addition, this system provides operating guidelines for optimal recirculation-gas control, enabling the reduction of NOx concentration in exhaust gas, since the plant can be operated in accordance with instruction procedures calculated by a multiple regression method.

articleTitle: Analysis Of Joint & Termination Failures On Extruded Dielectric Cables
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Instructions are presented in the proper methods of analyzing joint and termination failures on extruded dielectric cable. Causes of failure are discussed with relation to the failure paths they produce.

articleTitle: On the Evaluation of Mean Time Between Maintenances of Circuit Breakers for Industrial Plants
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The problem of a determination of the time intervals between two consecutive maintenances on circuit breakers is discussed.

articleTitle: Applications of Mutually Coupled Reactor
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A new device of mutually coupled series reactor is proposed. Analytical and experimental studies on the working models by using the miniature system are conducted. Effects on improvement of stability limits, suppression of fault currents, minimization of shaft torsional responses of the turbine generators, and control of the power flow in a power system are proved for the applications of the reactors.

articleTitle: Principles of a Water-Wheel Generator with Floating Rotor
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: In an axial-field vertical-shaft hydro-electric generator, magnetic pull can be utilized to support the rotating body and provide smooth starting and stopping. The magnetic flux densities in the generator's upper and lower airgaps are purposely made unequal by injecting unequal currents in its two field windings. In addition to other advantageous features which also justify the axial-field configuration, the floating rotor principle greatly simplifies the construction of the thrust bearing and its auxiliary mechanical system. Operations of turbine-generator sets will no longer be restricted by their bearing temperature as they are now with conventional units. An experimental machine was designed, constructed and tested.

articleTitle: A New Stored-Energy Vacuum Switch for Distribution System Automation
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: In the almost continual improvement in control and communications equipment, the switchgear aspect of operating an automated distribution system is frequently relegated to the background. To fully utilize advances in control and communications schemes, switch- gear must include correspondingly expanded capabilities. This paper discusses a new loadbreak switch that provides the capabilities necessary to automate fault- isolation as well as circuit-reconfiguration switching.

articleTitle: Development of a System for Field Testing of High Voltage Capacitors on Electrical Utility Systems With In-Circuit Measurement
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper addresses the development of systems to field test power factor correction capacitors in (1) Distribution type, group fused overhead installations, and (2) Substation type, individually fused in large banks.

articleTitle: Charging Large Capacitor Banks for Fusion Research Using HVDC Conversion Equipment
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Fundamental considerations in the choice of a continuous duty capacitor bank charging system using HVDC conversion equipment are presented. Large systems of the type used in fusion related research pose significant system related problems if they are to be supplied from a conventional power grid. Schemes for conditioning the required power in order to overcome such problems are presented and evaluated. A resonant charging system is examined in detail and shown to be superilor in a number of ways to constant current charging. Results of digital computer simulation studies are used to demonstrate the feasibility of the system. It is shown that the resonant charging system reduces rectifier capacity, simplifies control and reduces reactive power fluctuations. Sequential bank charging and use of a motor-generator set are presented as techniques for compensation of real power fluctuations and a comparison on the basis of initial cost is presented.

articleTitle: Technique for Determining Early Retirement of Distribution Transformers
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The calculation and evaluation of losses on electric utility systems are given increasing priority in decision making today because of the real increases in operating and plant costs, the importance of higher efficiency, and the continuing developments in various design technologies. This paper describes a method of analyzing the economic effects of the early retirement of distribution transformers considering the lower loss units available today.

articleTitle: The Polyphase Commutator Machine As A Wind Generator
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The polyphase commutator machine is recognized as a candiate for wind generation systems. This paper discusses the generating mode of this type of machine, in an attempt to define the practically feasible operating regions from the viewpoint of utilities anticipating an increase in the application of small wind generation.

articleTitle: Testing of a 1100 kV, 3 to 9 CVA Underground Transmission System
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: In the framework of the "1000-kV Project", it was agreed between ENEL and Societa Cavi Pirelli to carry out an extensive experimentation on an assembly including a 1100 kV self-contained, oil-filled cable and accessories, with a view to assess the reliability of such system intended for connections in power stations as well as for feeding areas with particular environmental constraints.

articleTitle: On Free Transient Convective Heat Transfer Between Cable and its Surrounding Pipe or Duct Wall
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The transient free convection heat transfer problem between cable and its enclosure is solved using the method of finite difference. As the transient time is found to be very small compared with a typical operation time, the steady state Nusselt number Can be used in lieu of the transient Nusselt number. Our numerical results are summarized in Fig. 9 which consists of three Nusselt number vs. Grashof number plots with diameter ratio as parameter and serves as a design chart for practical free convective heat transfer calculations.

articleTitle: The Dechlorination on Polychlorinated Biphenyls by Sodium Hydride and Alkylamine
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Polychlorinated biphenyls (PCBs) can be dechlorinated by using sodium hydride and alkylamine. The degree of dechlorination after reaction was determined by Gas Chromatography analysis. The concentration of PCBs can be reduced below 6 ppm when PCB contaminated mineral oil (in the range 400 ppm to 20,000 ppm) reacted with sodium hydride and ethylenediamine for 15 minutes from room temperature to 650C in air. The reaction is exothermic with the formation of sodium chloride, hydrogen and polymeric biphenylamine. A catalyzed nucleophilic displacement reaction was proposed for reaction mechanism. The reaction conditions are mild and simple. The reagents used are commonly available in commercial quantities. Therefore, this process may be feasible for commercial chemical destruction of PCBs.

articleTitle: Artificial Unloaded Lines for Testing High Voltage Circuit-Breakers
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The paper proposes various circuits which can be used to accurately simulate an unloaded electrical line or cable, and presents the results of tests performed on real and artificial lines.

articleTitle: Study of Fast Synchronous-Reclosing Method for Parallel AC Line Fault in AC/DC Poer Transmission System
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: In the AC/DC parallel system, AC power system is separated into two areas by the parallel AC line trip. As a result, it is necessary to recover from asynchronous operation. A method to close tripped AC line, "Fast synchronous-reclosing method", is proposed here. This paper consists of two parts: (1) Calculation of the frequency difference limit between the two areas. Energy function is formulated on the condition that fast synchronous-reclosing can be completed satisfactorily. (2) Confirmation of the performance of the fast synchronous-reclosing method in the AC/DC parallel line and frequency control before synchronous-reclosing and damping control of the power swing after reclosing, which were studied using an AC/DC simulator.

articleTitle: Marginal Cost Method for Deterministic Hydro Scheduling
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A new approach is presented, based on marginal cost methods, for solving the deterministic hydro-scheduling problem. The original dynamic scheduling problem is converted to a resource allocation problem. Several trajectory constraint rules are developed to guarantee the feasibility and optimality of the solution. The basic method is extended to multi-reservoir scheduling problems. These methods are shown to be very computationally efficient.

articleTitle: Techniques for Estimating Replacement Energy Values of Electrical Generating Units
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Evaluations of generating unit modifications often utilize replacement energy values which are much lower and less accurate than those obtained when economic dispatch and location of a unit in the dispatch sequence are considered, and the practice tends to denigrate the value of maintaining or improving plant productivity. A relatively simple technique is presented for properly accounting for the position of a unit in the dispatch order when estimating the replacement energy values for derating/uprating generation units. The actual utilization of the generation capacity segment added or lost is also included.

articleTitle: Testing and Commissioning of a Modular UHV AC Outdoor Test System
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: AEP's continuing research program in the area of UHV and EHV transmission led to the need for a 1200 kV, ac, outdoor test facility. An earlier paper describes the design and development of the 1200 kV test system. 1 In order to verify the test system's performance and obtain valuable operating information, a series of factory and field tests were conducted on the system and its components. This paper describes the results of these tests and the techniques used to gather the data. The use of a fiber- optic data acquisition system in the UHV environment is also described.

articleTitle: Reduction In Size And Weight Of Medium Voltage Switchgear
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The medium voltage switchgear have substantially been reduced in size and weight owing to the advance in insulation technology and strength analysis technique. Regarding the insulation technique this paper describes the use of barrier insulation and covering insulation and, with respect to the strength analysis, explains the application of a finite element method and a modal analysis method.

articleTitle: Recent Developments in HVDC Convertor Station Design
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: New requirements on HVDC convertor station performance have emerged during the past few years. The paper presents some of these requirements and shows how they have been met through equipment and system development. This development will result in a new generation of HVDC transmissions with still better performance than for the projects presently in operation.

articleTitle: Bulb Turbine/Generators for the Idaho Falls Hudroelectric Project
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Bulb turbines were used to rehabilitate three hydroelectric projects owned and operated by the City of Idaho Falls in Southeastern Idaho. The projects all have gross heads of approximately 5.8 meters (19 ft.) and are designed to utilize a flow of 170 cms (6,000 cfs). Because of the similarities of the sites, economy was achieved by purchase of three identical eight (8) megawatt units and designing each power- house the same. The physical arrangement of the structures differ slightly due to the variations in site geographies. Each plant is remotely operated and unmanned.

articleTitle: An Overview of the DC Wiring System Design Issues in the SMUD Phase I Photovoltaic Power Plant
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The DC wiring system of a photovoltaic power requires a number of safety features that result from the unique aspects of. photovoltaic devices. This paper presents an overview of the DC wiring system design developed for the Sacramento Municipal Utilities District (SMUD) Phase I photovoltaic power plant. The specific challenges that photovoltaic devices present to a power plant designer are identified along with the specific solutions adopted in the SMUD design.

articleTitle: Linear Voltage Regulation and Loss Calculation Methods for Low-Voltage Network Design
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A linear cost function is required to use in network design methods based on linear programming. The voltage regulation forms a constraint which should be taken into account in all design methods.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of the Field and Stray Losses df the End Bells of an Induction Motor
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The magnetic field on the surface of the end bell of a 10 HP induction motor is measured by Hall-effect probes and search coils under different test conditions. The losses are also measured. The results show that the leakage field and surface losses on the end bell are very small and have little effect on the efficiency and temperature rise of the machine.

articleTitle: Lightning Impulse Tests on Tower Models
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Lightning impulse tests on long insulator strings have been carried out in an attempt to determine the impulse strength of tower insulation in the EHV-UHV ranges.

articleTitle: A Case Study of an Underground PCB Spill: Fate of the Subsurface PCB Spill Residues and Its Imapct on Humans and the Environment
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A transformer located in a subsurface vault within the central business district of a city released PCB fluid which entered the ground through a french drain system in the vault floor. The present study was undertaken to examine if the subsurface PCB residues posed a risk to humans and the environment. Extensive data, gathered through field investigation and literature review on behavior of PCB in soils and water, were analyzed to determine the fate of the PCB residues and its potential impact on the environment. It was concluded that the subsurface PCB-contaminated soils could cause only a minor and highly localized contamination of the groundwater for a limited time period and did not pose a risk to humans or the environment.

articleTitle: A Study on the Improved Performance of Half-LENS-Half-MHO Relays
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: MHO type directional impedance relay has been widely used in HV and EHV systems for many years, but its misoperation under certain fault conditions has been a major problem. One such instance is that relays on unfaulted phases will misoperate during a close-in S-L-G fault with fault resistance. The other is the misoperation of MHO relay during a reverse fault with fault resistance.

articleTitle: Computation of Frequency of Right of Right-of-Way Losses Due to Tornadoes
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A mathematical model is presented for the computation of the frequency of a loss of right-of-way due to tornadoes. Relevant tornado characteristics are discussed.

articleTitle: Development Of Metal-Enclosed Switchgear Equipped With Automatic Dehumidifier
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Under contaminated and wet environment the insulation characteristic of the insulation surface in the switchgear deteriorates. The tracking and flashover characteristics of insulating materials for the indoor equipment were examined. Based on the result of the examination, a switchgear was developed which has a dehumidifier that automatically turns on to remove moisture only when the interior humidity is high. This system has proved very effective in improving the reliability of the switchgear.

articleTitle: Transit Sagging of Conductors using a Calculated Angle of Sight
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A method is developed to compute a transit vertical angle for the accurate sagging of long spans of aerial cables. The computation method is well suited to hand-held programmable calculators and allows the use of convenient transit locations.

articleTitle: Dead Tank Circuit Breaker Design Techniques
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A new dead tank circuit breaker has been developed with the manufacturing and testing advantages of the modular live tank circuit breaker concept. By locating the puffer interrupter inside the porcelain bushing it is possible to reduce the size of the single-phase breaker tank to the minimum required to support and insulate the main conductor and locate the circuit breaker bushings. Only one supporting insulator is used inside the tank for all the breaker components, and only one insulating operating rod bridges the gap from the tank to the main conductor. The rest of the insulation to earth is in gas and self-restoring.

articleTitle: Thermo-Mechanical Bending Effects In EHV Pipe-Type Cables
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper is a progress report on research funded jointly by the Electric Power Research Institute (EPRI) and the Empire State Electric Energy Research Corporation (ESEERCO), to investigate the EHV cable failure mechanism associated with Thermo-Mechanical Bending (TMB).

articleTitle: Electrical Features of the Wallace Dam Pumped Hydro Project
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The Wallace Dam Pumped Hydro Project was placed in full commercial operation in December 1980. This paper describes the significant features of this combination run-of-river and pumped storage project. Full-voltage, across-the-line starting is used for the 83,000 hp motors, making this the largest known unit using this starting method. The control system, using hard-wired, relay logic is also described.

articleTitle: Experience with end Enhancements to a Multinational Communications Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: In a paper published by IEEE in June 1983 (83-WM026-Z), the considerations given to establishing a multinational communications system were discussed. This paper discusses operating enhancements to the original system and expanded capabilities that are now being made a part of normal system operations.

articleTitle: Detection of PCB'S in Transformer Oil by Chlorine Analysis Field Experience
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Measurement of Polychlorinated Biphenyls (PCB's) in transformer oil is usually done in the laboratory, using the Gas Chromatograph (GC) with electron capture detector. This is a lengthy, expensive technique, performed only by trained, qualified laboratory technicians.

articleTitle: AC Auxiliary Power System Design for the Shoubrah El-Kheima Power Station
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper describes the design of the ac auxiliary power distribution system of a large multi-unit thermal power station located near Cairo, Egypt. The design features unitized auxiliary systems, shared start-up sources, and a combustion turbine-generator capable of feeding into each unit's electrical auxiliary system. The combustion turbine -generator is utilized both for black start of the station and to supply peaking power when required by the utility system. The auxiliary system configuration and the interrelationship of the design between units provide flexibility for operations and sufficient redundancy to ensure reliable sources of power for plant auxiliaries.

articleTitle: Analysis of Fiberglass Poles for Electric Power Distribution
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Developing countries need light-weight power distribution poles which resist deterioration in a hot, humid environment. It is possible that wound fiberglass poles can fill this need and also compete in industrialized countries with poles made of other materials. This paper presents an analysis of fiberglass power distribution poles. It is believed that the poles reported in this paper form the first such distribution line in the Western Hemisphere.

articleTitle: Progress Report of the Critical Equipment Monitoring System
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The Philadelphia Electric Company has contracted with Energy Data Systems to develop a Critical Equipment Monitoring System for its Peach Bottom Nuclear Plant. This computerized system is designed to acquire and maintain accurate and timely status information on plant equipment. It will provide auditable record of plant and equipment transactions. Positive equipment identification and location will be provided. Errors in complex logical checking will be minimized. This system should reduce operator loading and improve operator communicatin with the plant personnel.

articleTitle: Method of Comparative Measurement as a Survey Process to Determine the A-Weighted Sound Power Level of Rotating Electrical Machines
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The method suggested by the ISO/DP7849 document has been applied to. sixty three three phase induction machines. In the light of these experiments, and of some theoretical considerations, an alternative method is proposed, where the characteristic parameter of a machine is the product of a sound radiating surface by a radiating coefficient.

articleTitle: The Basic Principle and the Breaking Characteristics of the Composite Resistance Commutatiion Type DC Load Breaker
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: For the faults such as the grounding of DC transmission lines, the capability of DC breaker is only to be able to interrupt a load current because of the control functions of converter. So a simple interrupting system of DC load current is proposed here by making use of the composite resistance commutating system with three parallel circuits consisting of, a normally current passing electrode, a high voltage generating fusing element, and an energy dissipating non-linear resistance. This load breaker has suitable performance for high voltage interruption by using a multi-stage fusing element. For high current interruption a set of a gap in series to the fusing element is recommended.

articleTitle: "Retrofilling"-A Technique to Polychlorinated Biphenyls (PCBs)
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Mineral oil-filled transformers containing 500 ppm PCBs or greater are classified by the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) as PCB transformers. As such, these transformers are not allowed by EPA regulations to be rebuilt or internally serviced. By lowering the contamination level of PCBs below 500 ppm, the useful service life of these transformers may be extended since they would be reclassified as PCB-contaminated or non-PCB transformers, and internal servicing would be allowed. One means for accomplishing this reduction is retrofilling. The results of this study have been tabulated and guidelines have been specified to determine the suitability of a transformer to be retrofilled. This study reflects the effectiveness of retrofilling transformers to achieve reclassification

articleTitle: Equipment and Reliability Costs for Residential A/C Load Control: One-Way VS. Two-Way Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: When evaluating one-way versus two-way communication systems to perform the function of residential air conditioner load control as well as other load management functions, the costs associated with reliability should be considered and can be significant. A methodology is presented in this paper which can be used to evaluate the total equipment and reliabillty costs for both a one-way and two-way communication system.

articleTitle: The Application of Two-Out-of-Three Logic for the Control of Electric Motor Operated Valves in Candu safety Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Traditionally, the operation of electric motor operated (EMO) valves has been controlled by a position limit switch and a torque limit switch which are part of the actuator. A malfunction or improper maintenance of either of these switches has resulted in numerous actuator failures. The reliability of EMO valves and, in the case of nuclear power plants, the frequency of forced shutdowns could be significantly improved by using two-out-of-three logic in the control circuits. The feasibility of mounting additional switches on the valve and the control circuits was verified in tests and has been assessed as suitable for both new and existing nuclear installations.

articleTitle: SF6 Gas Insulated Load Interrupting Switches With Fusing
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper discusses the design and testing of an SF6, gas insulated load interrupting switch which has multiposition capability. The multiposition capability is achieved through the use of rotary switching contacts which allow a wide variety of switching arrangements within one enclosure.

articleTitle: A Regulatory Overview of Qualification of Equipment for Seismic and Dynamic Loads
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The generic problem areas which have most often been identified during the NRC staff review of equipment seismic and dynamic qualification programs for near term operating license plants are presented, in view of the current licensing acceptance criteria and plant site audit procedures.

articleTitle: "Criteria and Method for Specification and Evaluation of Distributed Digital Control Systems"
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Traditional methods of developing specifications and evaluating control systems have become less viable today, as a greater number of new Distributed Digital Systems become available.

articleTitle: Impedance and Loss Distribution of Multiple-Deck-Shaped Conductor with IDLE Loop in a Variable Width Slot
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: It is familiar that the calculation of the rotor-conductor deep-bar effect of an induction motor is well established.

articleTitle: Determination Of The Cleanliness Of High Voltage Insulation Compounds By A Laser Inspection Technique
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Since the cleanliness of high voltage insulation materials is essential for final cable quality, it is mandatory to qualify such products for their contamination level at the quality control stage of the material production.

articleTitle: Development of a Distribution Transformer Not Subject to Destructive Failure--An Update
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper reviews the application of a pancake coil winding in a 25 kVA, 15 kV class distribution transformer that is constructed using inorganic insulating materials. Techniques for designing transformers utilizing pancake coils have been developed and confirmed in full-size working models.

articleTitle: Installation and Operation of 600A Padmounted Deadfront Switchgear Wisconsin Electric Power Company's Experience
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Equipment is now available which provides maximum public and operator safety. Recent developments in the design of deadfront switchgear and associated terminations has resulted in deadfront padmounted switch-fuse units being available which meet the needs of Wisconsin Electric and many other electric utilities. This paper describes the design, installation, and operation of such equipment. Operating requirements, how they were determined and achieved are discussed. The information presented was obtained in a large part from field experience.

articleTitle: Six-Phase Transmission Systems: Capacitance Switching
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper is aimed at studying the capacitance switching phenomenon in a six-phase power transmission system and comparing it with that of a three-phase system. The study is conducted by first deriving the analytical expressions for the transient recovery voltages associated with capacitance switching for three representative situations, and then verifying these analytical results by simulating the six-phase system on the digital computer using an electromagnetic transients program. The results indicate that the capacitance switching imposes less onerous transient recovery voltages on a six-phase system when compared to a three-phase system.

articleTitle: Selection of Protective Coatings for Padmounted Equipment Maintenance
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A series of tests was performed on a number of protective coatings in order to select suitable maintenance coatings for padmounted electrical distribution equipment. Selection criteria, results of tests, and final selection are discussed. The test requirements of the proposed EEI guideline for protective coatings are also discussed in light of the results of the test program.

articleTitle: Deepwell Water System Control and Monitoring in a Nuclear Power Plant by Telemetry and Advanced Instrumentation
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The potable water in the Philippine Nuclear Power Plant is supplied by a network of ten interconnected deepwell turbine pumps. These underground submersible pumps are installed very deep in the ground. The region is hilly and large. Adequate protection of the expensive pumps, a high degree of automation, reliability and flexibility were the overall goals of the control and instrumentation. The advanced instrumentation consisted of: .digital control and digital monitoring. .a telemetry system for transmission of all signals between the master station and the ten satellite stations. .radiofrequency water level measturement in the wells.

articleTitle: Halogen-Free Fire Resistive Cable Splices
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Cables for power supplies, signals and communications have to be considered as very important and possibly weak points in the fire fighting and prevention systems. They rarely cause fires but may supply combustible material and assist flame propagation as they penetrate floors and walls.

articleTitle: Utility Load Management Organization Survey
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The IEEE Load Management Working Grout (currently Load Management Subcommittee) of the Power System Engineering Committee commissioned a task force to study utility load management organizational structure. This Task Force conducted a survey of 20 utilities and examined relationships between organization, objectives, types of programs, and stage of program development. This paper suarizes the survey results. One interesting resul t was that utilities with larger 1990 MW goals for load management tended to have a Vice President of rates, marketing, or conservation overseeing load management. Moreover, these utilities tended to have a seDarate, identifiable load management planning group.

articleTitle: Design And Testing Of 270kV D. C. Self-Contained, Oil-Filled Cable For The Land Section Of The UK-France Connection
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Self-contained, oil-filled cable has been chosen for the land section of the 2000 MW, 270kV d. c. system which is to link together the 400kV a. c. transmission systems of France and the United Kingdom [1], [2].

articleTitle: The New Venezuelan National Control Center
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper describes the actual status of the Venezuelan Electric Power System, the different operacional areas involved, and finally the Interconnected System.

articleTitle: Modeling Intermittent Generation (IG) in a Monte-Carlo Regional System Analysis Model
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A simulation model capable of simulating the operation of a given load/resource scenario is developed under the umbrella of PNUCC's System Analysis Committee [1, 2]. This model, called System Analysis Model (SAM), employs the Monte-Carlo technique to incorporate quantifiable uncertainties. Explicit uncertainties in SAM include: hydro conditions, load forecast errors, construction duration, availability of thermal units, renewable resources (wind, solar, geothermal, and biomass), cogeneration, and conservation.

articleTitle: Equipment Qualification: The Process for New Plants as Seen by a Utility
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The qualification process, based on the experience an electric utility gained through its efforts to meet the requirements of IEEE Standards 627-80 and 323-1974 and the attendant regulatory guidance for new plants, is presented. Important aspects of each step from initial plant design to maintaining equipment qualification during operations are described. Although all these steps are not directly applicable to near-term and operating plants, the guidance offered is generally appropriate for procurement of qualified spare and replacement parts and for plant modifications of safety systems.

articleTitle: Optimal Power Flow By Newton Approach
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The classical optimal power flow problem with a nonseparable objective function can be solved by an explicit Newton approach. Efficient, robust solutions can be obtained for problems of any practical size or kind. Solution effort is approximately proportional to network size, and is relatively independent of the number of controls or binding inequalities. The key idea is a direct simultaneous solution for all of the unknowns in the Lagrangian function on each iteration. Each iteration minimizes a quadratic approximation of the Lagrangian. For any given set of binding constraints the process converges to the Kuhn-Tucker conditions in a few iterations. The challenge in algorithm development is to efficiently identify the binding inequalities.

articleTitle: Quadratically Convergent Optimal Power Flow
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: A newly developed sparse implementation of an optimization method using exact second derivatives is applied to the optimal power flow problem. Four utility systems are studied using a variety of objective functions, including fuel costs, active and reactive losses, and new shunt capacitors. Systems solved range from 350 buses to 2000 buses. Comparisons are made with an older algorithm which uses an Augmented Lagrangian to demonstrate the advantages of run time and robustness of the new method. The algorithm and accompanying software represent a technological breakthrough, since they are suitable for solving systems on the order of 2000 buses and demonstrate solution speeds of 5 minutes on large mainframe computers. The method is particularly well suited to infeasible, or even divergent starting points. An option to add shunt capacitors in the event of hopeless infeasibility guarantees an optimal solution for many difficult to solve systems. An automatic scaling feature is added to correct numerical ill-conditioning resulting from series compensation or poor R/X ratios.

articleTitle: Optimal Estimation Of Voltage Phasors And Frequency Deviation Using Linear And Non-Linear Kalman Filtering: Theory And Limitations
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper presents two techniques for optimal tracking of power system voltage phasors and frequency deviation. The first technique is based on a two-state linear Kalman filter model. The second technique is based on a three-state extended Kalman filter model. In the latter the frequency deviation is considered a third state variable and is recursively computed on-line. It is shown that the Kalman filter models are well suited for noisy measurements. The effect of sampling rate, computer burden and overall accuracy are also investigated. Finally comparison with other techniques is presented.

articleTitle: Power System Stabilizer Based on Adaptive Control Techniques
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Characteristics of certain adaptive control techniques are discussed in this paper with particular emphasis on their application to power systems. A modified form of one of the more promising algorithms that makes it more suitable. for power systems is developed and described. Comparative results of studies with adaptive stabilizer based on two alternate adaptive control algorithms and a conventional fixed parameter stabilizer show the improvement in response obtained with the adaptive algorithm.

articleTitle: Analytical Modelling of Grounding Electrodes Transient Behavior
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper presents the results of analytical and numerical investigations to evaluate the impulse performance of grounding electrodes. Practical grounding electrodes used-for the lightning protection of power and industrigl systems are analyzed through, a comprehensive computer program developed for this purpose. The validity of the proposed methodology has been verified with various data available in the literature. Reaiistic models of grounding electrodes involve non-linear admittance elements which here are replaced with a pie% ewise-linear approach as a result of an artificial electrode segmentation.

articleTitle: Probabilistic Load Flow Considering Dependence Between Input Nodal Powers
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper presents a new method for obtaining a probabilistic load flow solution when dependence between the input nodal powers is considered. Such dependence is modeled in order to account for the criteria used to balance the system active power and also the correlation between loads due-mainly to environmental and social factors. The proposed technique is applied to a typical power system and the results discussed.

articleTitle: Lightning Induced Voltages on Power Lines: Theory
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Theory is presented which shows that nearby lightning return strokes can induce voltage surges of either positive or negative polarity on an overhead line depending on the location of the lightning relative to the line. The Telegraphers' Equations are solved with the return stroke vertical and horizontal electric fields as forcing functions. The hori zontal electric fields are calculated from measured or assumed vertical fields and assuned earth conductivities. For a typical return stroke, voltage waveforms are presented for a line of 500 m length and one of 5 km length for the following conditions: earth conductivities between 10-2 mhos/m and 10-5 mhos/m, earth permittivities between εϒ= 15 and εϒ= 3, and lightning ground strike points between 0.2 km and 5.0 km of the line at a variety of positions around the line. Measured voltages on a 460 m test line described in a companion paper are compared with calculated voltage waveforms derived from measured vertical electric fields, in accordance with the developed theory. Calculated waveshapes are found to be in moderately good agreement with the measurements, but calculated magnitudes are about a factor of 4 lower than measured. Possible errors in both theory and measurement are discussed. Voltage measurements reported by other investigators are, in general, consistent with the present theory

articleTitle: Computer Aided Transmission Protection System Design Part I: Alcorithms
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The role of a computer-aided-design tool in assisting protection engineers is defined. In the process, we identify three computational problems for which algorithms are not readily available: network analysis to find primary/backup relay pairs, setting directional overcurrent relays and setting distance relays. Suitable algorithms for each of these tasks are presented.

articleTitle: Application of a Thyristor Controlled Var Compensator for Damping Subsynchronous Oscillations in Power Systems
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper presents a new concept for controlling static VAr compensators (SVC) in power systems. It allows thyristor controlled VAr compensators to effectively damp subsynchronous resonance (SSR) oscillations besides controlling the system voltage. Eigenvalue analysis and digital time simulations for the IEEE SSR benchmark system are utilized to investigate the role of the main voltage regulator of the SVC in stabilizing the system and alleviating the SSR modal interactions that may be introduced by the auxiliary speed signal alone. Stability zones are identified to optimize the compensator parameters for economical application.

articleTitle: Computer-Aided Planning of Distribution Substation and Primary Feeders
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: This paper presents an improved technique for optimal planning of substations and primary feeders in power distribution systems. The technique employs an accurate, time-phased cost model and incorporates a flexible planning formulation which suits detailed analysis of limited sized distribution networks as well as approximate analysis of large scale distribution networks. The cost model includes explicit time-dependent fixed and variable charges for planned facilities as well as the cost of power losses. The planning formulation incorporates user-defined constraints on voltage drop in primary feeders. Constraints on radial power flow are automatically set by the algorithm. The planning problem is solved using an advanced, sparsity-based mixed-integer linear programming code.

articleTitle: Lightning Induced Voltages on Power Lines: Experiment
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: We present correlated measurements of the voltage induced on a power line by nearby lightning and the vertical electric field intensity from that lightning. Data are given for more than 100 first strokes and more than 200 subsequent strokes with the lightning ground strike point located by triangulation using a network of television cameras and by thunder ranging. Voltages were measured at one end of a 460 m unenergized distribution line which was open-circuited at both ends. A neutral wire was located beneath the line and was grounded at both ends. The time-domain voltaqe and vertical electric field waveforms were detected and recorded on a system having a frequency response from less than 1 Hz to over 1 MHz. Only about half of the vol tage waveforms resemble the "classical induced positive surges" described in the literature. The magnitude and polarity of the peak induced voltage is a strong function of the location of the lightning ground strike point.

articleTitle: A Method to Teach the Design and Operation of a Distribution System
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The undergraduate "power option" program at New Mexico State University consists of five courses. Of these five, one is required of all electrical engineering majors, one is a "block elective" and three are senior electives. The "block elective" is a method by which an electrical engineering major must select three courses from a list of six. The list includes one course in each of the six "option" areas offered by the department. The five power courses are: 1. Electric Machinery -------- required of all majors 2. Power Transmission Lines -- "block elective" 3. Power Systems Analysis ---- senior elective 4. Distribution Systems ------ senior elective 5. Power System Protection --- senior elective

articleTitle: Earth Resistivity Measurement Interpretation Techniques
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: Earth resistivity measurement interpretation techniques developed as part of a major EPRI research project on transmission line grounding are described and discussed. The interpretation techniques include graphical curve matching and an advanced computer program (RESIST). The curve matching technique requires a set of theoretical Master Curves with which a field curve can be compared directly. Program RESIST is based on the analytical methods used in a more elaborate computer program which has been in operation for several years. For an electrode spacing of 2.5 meters or greater, satisfactory agreement is obtained between measured and computed results using both interpretation techniques.

articleTitle: Bound Estimates of the Severity of Line Outages in Power System Contingency Analysis and Ranking
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The effect of line outages on the real power flows of a system is analyzed using the DC load flow model. It is shown that the effect of the out4ge of line jk on the power flow of an arbitrary line lm can be bounded above and below by a series of progressively tighter values which in the limit correspond to the exact DC load flow solution. The calculation of these bound estimates on the contingency line flows is progressively more computationally demanding as the limits tighten, however, the simple to compute bounds, although more conservative, still serve to filter out a large portion of the non-critical contingencies. The remaining few potentially critical outages can then be ranked and analyzed through the full DC load flow.

articleTitle: Hypothesis Testing Identification: A New Method For Bad Data Analysis In Power System State Estimation
publicationTitle: IEEE Transactions on Power Apparatus and Systems
abstract: The anomalous data identification procedures existing today in power system state estimation become problematic-if not totally unefficient-under stringent conditions, such as multiple and interacting bad data. The identification method presented in this paper attempts to alleviate these difficulties.
